title: Natural Domain and Graph of y = sqrt(-x)
originalTopic: Functions and Graphs: Domain and Graphing
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Find the natural domain and describe the graph of the function g(x) = sqrt(-x).

steps.title: Set Up the Radicand Inequality
steps.explanation: For sqrt(-x) to be a real number, the radicand -x must be non-negative. Multiplying both sides of -x >= 0 by -1 reverses the inequality to give x <= 0.
steps.why: When x is negative or zero, its negation -x is positive or zero.

steps.title: State the Natural Domain
steps.explanation: The natural domain consists of zero and all negative real numbers.
steps.why: Any positive input x > 0 makes the radicand -x negative, which has no real square root.

steps.title: Describe the Graph via Reflection
steps.explanation: The graph is the reflection of y = sqrt(x) across the y-axis. It starts at the origin (0, 0) and rises to the left into the second quadrant, passing through (-1, 1) and (-4, 2).
steps.why: Replacing x with -x in a function formula reflects its graph horizontally across the y-axis.
